question: Should OpenClaw add a generic action-aware tool-policy contract for multiplexed tools, and what trusted bypass semantics should approved workflows use?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear in source, but the fix defines a new authorization boundary and public config grammar across message, gateway, sender, sandbox, plugin, and HTTP invocation paths.

options.title: Design Generic Action Policy
options.body: Add a typed action-aware policy grammar enforced before multiplexed tool actions execute, with documented precedence and trusted-context tests for message and gateway.

options.title: Narrow To Known Tools
options.body: Add separate action controls only for the current message and gateway cases, reducing immediate scope but creating parallel policy surfaces that may drift.

options.title: Defer To Approval Work
options.body: Use the adjacent confirmation or approval-resolver direction for human approval and accept that static least-privilege action deny remains unavailable for now.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Action Policy
recommendation.body: Add a typed action-aware policy grammar enforced before multiplexed tool actions execute, with documented precedence and trusted-context tests for message and gateway.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the clearest routing candidate from the live issue discussion and prior policy/message/gateway review context.
